transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I’ve been way more driven and wired than usual for weeks, like I can’t slow down or stop starting new projects, and now it’s starting to blow up my job. HR actually insisted I come get evaluated before I can go back to work because things have gotten so out of hand.
Have you ever experienced a period in the past where you felt significantly depressed, sad, or hopeless for two weeks or longer?

Yes, for about the last four months I've been feeling incredibly down, guilty, and checked-out, especially as things at work started falling apart. These heavy feelings have been pretty constant, and on the bad days I even catch myself wishing I just wouldn't wake up. It's been going on like that consistently during this time.

During these periods when you feel incredibly driven or wired, have you ever experienced things that others couldn't see or hear, or held beliefs that felt undeniably true to you even when others insisted they weren't?

Yes, when I'm up late working, I keep hearing a deep, calm voice telling me I’ve been chosen to "wake up" the Providence economy and that my clients are secretly testing me. I also became convinced I had a special, grand role to transform the whole waterfront. These voices and beliefs only started happening once I got extremely wired and sleep-deprived after my promotion.

latest_inference.note: The patient reports a period of elevated mood, increased goal-directed activity, and decreased need for sleep, accompanied by psychotic features (auditory hallucinations and delusions of grandeur). This meets the criteria for a manic episode with psychotic features. Given the report of a preceding four-month depressive episode, the diagnosis of Bipolar I Disorder with current manic episode and psychotic features is the most appropriate, narrowing the candidates from F31.1 (manic without psychosis) to F31.2 (manic with psychosis).
